title_en: GSAM’s Lake, Innovator’s Day on Active Outcomes
title_zh: GSAM 的 Byron Lake 与 Innovator 的 Graham Day 谈"结果导向"的主动管理
description: As investors increasingly focus on managing risk, generating income and achieving specific portfolio outcomes, the definition of successful active management is expanding beyond simply outperforming a benchmark. In this episode of the Inside Active podcast, host David Cohne, mutual fund and active management analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, speaks with Bryon Lake, global co-head of third-party wealth and chief transformation officer at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, and Graham Day, partner and chief investment officer at Innovator from Goldman Sachs Asset Management, about how that shift is reshaping active strategies. They explore the growth of active and defined-outcome ETFs, why the traditional active-versus-passive debate may be giving way to a more solutions-oriented approach, and how derivatives can help investors customize risk, income and downside protection. They also discuss the importance of advisor education as product innovation accelerates, the role of technology and data in active management, and why fixed income could be the next major area of ETF innovation. Recorded Aug. 4.

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers that goes beyond sound bites and headlines and looks steeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection. I'm David Cone, I, lead mutual fund and active research of Bloomberg Intelligence. For decades, active success was often measured by one question, did a manager outperform a benchmark? While performance remains essential, invests today are increasingly asking different questions about risk, income and how active strategies fit within broader portfolios. Those changing expectations are reshaping not only how active managers invest, but also how they design strategies and measure success. So today I wanted to explore how the definition of active management is evolving, what's driving innovations us the industry, and what active managers will need to do differently to remain relevant over the next decade. Joining me to discuss that Brian Lake, Global co head of Third Party Wealth and Chief Transformation Officer at gold min Sex and Graham day partner and Chief Investment Officer at Innovator ETFs from Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Brian Graham, thank you both for joining me. Nice to see David going to be here. So, Brian, active management has evolved significantly over the past five years. What do you think is the single biggest change you've seen? And you know why do you think that matters? Yeah?
turns.zh: 欢迎收听《Inside Active》，这是一档探讨主动管理人（active manager）的播客。节目不止停留在只言片语和新闻标题，而是更深入地了解他们在证券选择（security selection）方面的投资流程（investment process）、挑战和投资理念（investment philosophy）。我是 David Cone，负责 Bloomberg Intelligence 的共同基金（mutual fund）及主动研究。几十年来，衡量主动管理是否成功，往往只看一个问题：管理人有没有跑赢业绩基准（benchmark）？业绩仍然至关重要，但如今投资者越来越多地提出与风险、收益，以及主动策略如何融入更广泛投资组合有关的不同问题。这些不断变化的期望不仅在重塑主动管理人的投资方式，也在改变他们设计策略和衡量成功的方式。因此，今天我想探讨主动管理（active management）的定义正在如何演变、什么因素正在推动整个行业的创新，以及主动管理人要想在未来十年继续保持相关性，需要采取哪些不同做法。今天与我共同讨论的是 Goldman Sachs Asset Management 全球第三方财富管理联席主管兼首席转型官 Brian Lake，以及 Goldman Sachs Asset Management 旗下 Innovator ETFs 的合伙人兼首席投资官 Graham Day。Brian、Graham，感谢二位参加节目。David，很高兴见到你，也很高兴来到这里。那么 Brian，主动管理在过去五年里发生了显著演变。你看到的最大单一变化是什么？你认为它为什么重要？

turns.en: Well, first of all, David, thanks for having us that. It's always a pleasure to chat with you. You know, I think your question is a good one because you know, what I like to do is kind of invert the question. And you even said this in the intro. It's a little bit less about an arbitrary performance from January first to December thirty first, and more what is the investor trying to accomplish within their portfolio. And so even though we have this big phrase active, I think what we're really focused on is investor outcomes. And so within the ETF space, active ets now comprise about ten percent of assets. And when you look into that, what you're starting to see is that the different types of categories in there are very interested and indeed oriented toward client outcomes. The income strategy derivative income where you see strategies like gpick and gpicks that are designed to give investors income on a regular basis, or the defined outcome strategy buffer strategy like with the Innovator suite of products. Those also give investors a defined outcome or some sort of a downside protection or a floor. And so the biggest evolution that we've seen in active is less around simple risk adjusted return across the defined kind of arbitrary period and more about investors' outcomes and what they're actually trying to accomplish within their portfolios.
turns.zh: 首先，David，谢谢你邀请我们。和你交流总是很愉快。我认为这个问题问得很好，因为我喜欢把问题反过来看。正如你在开场时所说，现在的重点已不再那么侧重于从 1 月 1 日到 12 月 31 日这一任意期间内的业绩，而更多在于投资者希望通过自己的投资组合实现什么。尽管我们使用“主动”这个宽泛的说法，但我认为我们真正关注的是投资者结果。在交易所交易基金（exchange-traded fund, ETF）领域，主动型交易所交易基金（active ETF）目前约占资产规模的 10%。深入观察后，你会开始发现，其中不同类别都非常关注客户结果，实际上也是围绕客户结果设计的。比如收益策略和衍生品收益策略，其中有 GPIX 和 GPIQ 这类旨在定期为投资者提供收益的策略；又比如 Innovator 产品系列中的确定结果型 ETF（defined-outcome ETF）策略和缓冲型 ETF（buffer ETF）策略，它们也会给投资者带来确定的结果，或某种下行保护（downside protection）或保底线。因此，我们看到主动管理最大的演变，并不是简单考察某个明确但有些任意的期间内的风险调整后收益（risk-adjusted return），而是关注投资者结果，以及他们真正希望在投资组合中实现什么。

turns.en: Makes sense, Graham, But how about you the same question?
turns.zh: 很有道理。Graham，你怎么看同一个问题？

turns.en: Yeah, David, I would say, similar to Brian, we've seen just an explosion, explosive growth within drivetive based ETFs, and I think one of the things that we're going to continue to see is this evolution of how how can I drive client outcomes using these derivatives. They allow you to customize the level of risk that you're willing to take, or customize how much income you're wanting to get. And I think a lot of this is all a fall out of twenty twenty two when you had stocks and bonds going down together and then people started realizing, what can I use to protect my portfolio that isn't interest rate tied? What else can I use to drive higher levels of income that again isn't necessarily associated just with bonds, and so I think this has really opened up Pandora's box in a good and from our perspective, we love bringing new products to market, but I think you're going to continue to see more evolution within this derivative based ETF segment of the market. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的，David。与 Brian 的看法类似，我们看到基于衍生品（derivatives）的 ETF 出现了爆发式增长。我认为，我们将继续看到的一项演变是：如何利用这些衍生品来实现客户结果。它们允许你定制自己愿意承担的风险水平，或定制自己希望获得的收益金额。我认为，这在很大程度上都是 2022 年股债齐跌所产生的结果。人们随后开始意识到，我可以用什么来保护投资组合，而且不与利率挂钩？我还可以用什么来获得更高水平的收益，而且同样不一定只与债券相关？因此，我认为这打开了潘多拉魔盒，但这是件好事。从我们的角度来看，我们乐于把新产品推向市场。我认为，在 ETF 市场基于衍生品的这一细分领域，你将继续看到更多演变。

turns.en: Well, there's definitely a lot of interest. We've been tracking interest in these products for a while, so it's kind of fun to watch. And Brian, you've worked across multiple leading asset managers, some of the biggest changes in the industry have occurred. Looking back over your career, what's one belief about active management you've changed your mind about.
turns.zh: 确实有很多人感兴趣。我们跟踪这些产品受到的关注已经有一段时间了，所以观察它们的发展也颇有意思。Brian，你曾在多家领先的资产管理公司（asset manager）任职，亲历了行业中一些最重大的变化。回顾你的职业生涯，对于主动管理，有哪一种看法是你后来改变了的？

turns.en: Well, I mean, you know, I think the biggest thing, David is if you if you see how investors are accessing active management. You know, increasingly the ETF vehicle has become the delivery mechanism that investors are using. And you know, initially ETFs delivered Plaintanilla pass it or market cap weighted BEATA and over time, what investors have acknowledged is that the ETF rapper comes with a lot of benefits itself. It trades throughout the day, it's transparent, it has some tax efficient features, it tends to allow flexibility for investors to get selection across different different exposures. And when you can take some of the best active capabilities and deliver it through the ETF technology, you've got the combination of how investors access that with the investment engine that goes along with that, and so, you know, I think there's a really attractive spectrum that has developed for investors to choose the different vehicles that they want in the different exposures that they want to build the outcomes that they want specifically for their portfolios. So I don't know so much that it's a surprise as much it is as it is the flexibility and ability for investors to choose amongst thousands of ETFs to build the perfect exposures that they're looking for.
turns.zh: 我认为最重要的一点是，David，如果观察投资者获取主动管理的方式，就会发现 ETF 工具越来越成为他们采用的交付机制。最初，ETF 提供的是普通的被动投资（passive investing），也就是市值加权（market-cap weighting）的贝塔（beta）；但随着时间推移，投资者认识到，ETF 载体（ETF wrapper）本身就具备很多优势。它可以在日内交易，透明度高，具有一定的税务效率（tax efficiency）优势，通常还让投资者可以灵活选择不同的投资敞口。如果能够把一些最优秀的主动管理能力通过 ETF 技术交付出去，就能把投资者获取这些能力的方式与背后的投资引擎结合起来。因此，我认为，目前已经形成了一个非常有吸引力的选择谱系，投资者可以选择自己想要的不同工具和不同敞口，从而构建专门适合自身投资组合的预期结果。与其说这令我意外，不如说真正值得关注的是，投资者可以从数千只 ETF 中进行选择，灵活地构建自己所寻求的理想敞口。

turns.en: So, if we go a step further, you know, just thinking of the way investors and advisors think about products. You know, Graham, as CIO, you've helped develop investment strategies designed to meet a range of investor objectives. Do you think the definition of successful active management is changing for investors and advisors?
turns.zh: 如果再进一步，思考一下投资者和顾问看待产品的方式。Graham，作为首席投资官，你参与开发了旨在满足一系列投资者目标的投资策略。你认为，对投资者和顾问来说，成功的主动管理的定义正在改变吗？

turns.en: Yeah, David, I think could to borrow from what you said at the ONSET, it used to be about help performing a benchmark, and I think what people have realized is that active management can mean a lot more than that it can meet, as Brian was saying, achieving client outcomes in ways that had never been available before. We look at some of our strategies like a dual directional ETF, it's considered an actively managed strategy, and with that you can know exactly how much upside potential you have in a positive market. You also know how much inverse potential you have in a negative market, meaning if the market is down ten or fifteen percent over a one year time frame. You can actually make money with these types of strategies. And it's allowing advisors to understand that it's really not necessarily about beating the benchmark in up years. It's being able to control those client outcomes because they have to go and talk to their clients and say, hey, look, we don't know what's going to happen in the future. Twenty twenty two might happen again, stocks and bonds go down together. We need solutions that are prepared that for any market, and our interest rates go up if they go down, we need to have solutions that are going to withstand any of those market environments, and so those are the types of solutions that we're looking to build, are balanced within portfolio that are going to be tried and true regardless of the market environment.
turns.zh: 是的，David。借用你开场时的说法，过去关注的是跑赢业绩基准。我认为，人们已经意识到主动管理可以意味着更多。正如 Brian 所说，它可以用过去从未有过的方式实现客户结果。以我们的一些策略为例，比如双向 ETF，它被视为一种主动管理策略。借助这种产品，你可以确切知道市场上涨时自己拥有多少上涨潜力，也知道市场下跌时自己拥有多少反向收益潜力。也就是说，如果市场在一年期内下跌 10% 或 15%，你实际上可以通过这类策略赚钱。这让顾问明白，关键未必是在上涨年份跑赢业绩基准，而是能够掌控客户结果，因为他们必须对客户说：“我们不知道未来会发生什么。2022 年的情况可能重演，股票和债券可能一起下跌。我们需要能够为任何市场环境做好准备的解决方案。无论利率上升还是下降，我们都需要能够承受任何这类市场环境的解决方案。”因此，我们希望构建的，正是能够在投资组合中发挥平衡作用、无论市场环境如何都经得住考验的解决方案。

turns.en: Okay, you know, Brian, you had mentioned, you know, obviously ETF is kind of the preferred rapper and we've seen you know, active ETFs now tracting record assets and you know flows, And do you think that is primarily a story about the rapper itself or do you think investors demand for active management itself is actually fundamentally changed.
turns.zh: 好的。Brian，你刚才提到，ETF 显然可以说是首选载体；我们也看到主动型 ETF 如今吸引了创纪录的资产规模和资金流。你认为这主要是载体本身的故事，还是投资者对主动管理的需求本身已经发生了根本变化？

turns.en: Well, I think Graham said it perfectly. As you as you expand the definition of what active actually means, it certainly plays into that in a big way. And so I would agree completely with Graham, and I think that kind of answers your question of once you reframe and widen the aperture of what active management means and you can deliver some of the outcomes that investors are looking for, that that client adoption and investor adoption is is just going to continue to increase as they can express their views on the markets in a number of different ways.
turns.zh: 我认为 Graham 说得非常准确。随着你扩展主动管理实际含义的定义，它无疑会在很大程度上推动这一趋势。因此，我完全赞同 Graham 的观点。我认为这也回答了你的问题：一旦你重新界定并拓宽主动管理含义的范围，而且能够实现投资者寻求的某些结果，那么随着投资者能够以多种不同方式表达自己对市场的看法，客户采用和投资者采用就只会继续增加。

turns.en: Okay, So but if we go one step further, Brian, you know, we've spent years debating active vers passive and you know, throughout my career this has been a big thing. Do you think it's still the right debate or should investors actually be asking a different question now?
turns.zh: 好的。但如果再进一步，Brian，多年来我们一直在争论主动与被动；在我的整个职业生涯中，这始终是一个重大话题。你认为这仍然是正确的争论吗？还是投资者现在其实应该提出另一个问题？

turns.en: Look, I think the best portfolio is on both active and passive, and I think that changes in different market environments. I think that changes in different asset classes. I think that changes in different regions around the world. There's definitely times where maybe passive makes some sense. I think there's times where active makes sense. What I think we're actually touching on is in these subcategories of active where you have either income based strategies or you have buffer based strategies. Those are giving you, as the name implies, the defined outcome. If you want to give yourself a buffer of ten or fifteen percent to the downside, you can understand what the ETF is going to do to deliver that piece. And so that's more how I think investors are thinking about it these days is they have this variety of tools that they can use, and it's less around an arbitrary active versus passive and more around what am I trying to accomplish in my portfolio and what are the tools available for me to do that.
turns.zh: 我认为，最佳投资组合会同时持有主动和被动产品，而且二者的搭配会随不同市场环境而变化，也会随不同资产类别以及全球不同地区而变化。有些时候，被动投资或许有道理；另一些时候，主动管理更合适。我认为，我们实际谈到的是主动管理下的这些子类别：有的是收益型策略，有的是缓冲型策略。顾名思义，它们会给你带来确定的结果。如果你希望为下跌设置 10% 或 15% 的下行缓冲（downside buffer），就可以了解这只 ETF 将如何实现这一点。因此，如今投资者更多是这样思考的：他们有各种各样可以使用的工具。重点不再是任意地争论主动还是被动，而是我想在投资组合中实现什么，以及有哪些工具可以帮助我做到这一点。

turns.en: These type of products or you know, as I mentioned before, they're gaining momentum. But Graham, do you think the industry still puts too much emphasis on upperforming benchmarks.
turns.zh: 这类产品——正如我之前提到的——正在获得发展势头。不过 Graham，你认为行业仍然过度强调跑赢业绩基准吗？

turns.en: You know, I don't know if the maybe the industry does, David, I don't think advisors do. I think they to what we're discussing here. They are more interested in finding solutions, whether that's if there if their portfolio is mainly building blocks of passive beta instruments S and P five hundred NASDAQ one hundred. But when a client comes in and says, hey, look I just sold my business and now I've got all this money that I've worked twenty years for, what are we going to do with it? The advisor can't just say let's just put it in these passive building blocks. Because they know that they have one hundred percent of downside risk. They need tools that they can come to the client and say, hey, look, I know you've worked twenty years for this. We have a way to give you some of the market up side, but we're also going to be protecting that money that you have worked twenty years for that's not available with the past building blocks that are out there today. So you need to extend your purview beyond just the beta building blocks, because what you're going to find is these are real life solutions. There are solutions that solve problems that advisors are facing with their clients every day. Another one is we've talked at length with advisors and other industry experts on is this idea of well, what do you do if you've got all this cash on the sidelines. If you have cash on the sidelines, you want one hundred percent protection, that's why you're in cash. Well, there have to be other ways to be able to get that cash up the sidelines. What you find is a lot of these advisors their clients has just said, look, I don't really care, I don't want to take any risk. Well we come and say, well, we have these hundred percent offer ETFs. You have no doubtside. Now the market has to go up in order for you to make money, but this principle that you have about not wanting to lose any money, it's still there. And so these are the kind of the evolution, just these tools that we're able to build that extend beyond these passive building blocks that allow people to get invested in the market to maybe increase their risk tolerance so that they're not overweight fixed income, they're not overweight cash in ways that don't align with their long term investment goals. And so I think that's what we're going to continue to see, is this education, this evolution, and how advisors are using these new building blocks to pair with what they've been using for decades and again in a more client solution oriented manner.
turns.zh: David，我不知道行业或许是不是这样，但我认为顾问不是。正如我们一直在讨论的，他们更有兴趣寻找解决方案。他们的投资组合可能主要由被动贝塔工具构成，比如 S&P 500、Nasdaq-100。但如果有位客户前来说：“我刚刚卖掉自己的企业，现在手里有这么一大笔钱，这是我辛苦工作 20 年赚来的。我们该怎么处理？”顾问不能只是说，那就把钱都放进这些被动投资基础模块。因为他们知道，这样要承担 100% 的下行风险。他们需要有工具，可以对客户说：“我知道这是你辛苦工作 20 年积累下来的。我们有办法让你获得一部分市场上涨收益，同时也会保护你这 20 年辛苦赚来的钱。”如今已有的被动投资基础模块无法做到这一点。因此，你需要把视野扩展到贝塔基础模块之外，因为你会发现，这些都是现实生活中的解决方案，解决的是顾问每天面对客户时遇到的问题。另一个我们与顾问和其他行业专家深入讨论过的问题是：如果场外还有大量现金，该怎么办？如果你把现金放在场外，就是想获得 100% 保护，这正是你持有现金的原因。那么，一定还要有其他办法把这些现金调动起来。你会发现，很多顾问的客户只是说：“我真的不在乎，我不想承担任何风险。”而我们会说：“我们有这些提供 100% 缓冲的 ETF，你没有下行损失。市场现在必须上涨，你才能赚钱；但你不想损失任何资金的这一原则仍然得到了保留。”因此，这就是我们能够构建的工具的演变。这些工具超越了被动投资基础模块，能够让人们投资市场，也许还能提高他们的风险承受能力，从而避免以不符合长期投资目标的方式超配固定收益（fixed income）或超配现金。我认为，我们将继续看到这种教育和演变，也会看到顾问如何把这些新的基础模块与沿用了几十年的模块搭配使用，并再次以更加面向客户解决方案的方式使用它们。

turns.en: So when you're building these products, you know, what is putting together an active strategy like this around an objective? Is it requires something different than building one to simply outperform a benchmark.
turns.zh: 那么，在构建这些产品时，围绕某个目标打造这样的主动策略，与打造一个只是为了跑赢业绩基准的策略相比，是否需要不同的东西？

turns.en: You know, in a lot of ways, it's borrowing from both worlds. It's taking this idea of what active management has maybe done in the past or what they have attempted to deliver, and then marrying it with what AID is known for rules based systematic Those two can come together in a ways that we think are more powerful in delivering those outcomes for clients and their advisors. So I think it's really just being able to look across and say we can take from both of these worlds, put them together and deliver better solutions for advisors. And their clients.
turns.zh: 在很多方面，这是在借鉴两个领域。它采用主动管理过去或许做过、或曾试图交付的东西，再把它与 ETF 所擅长的基于规则的系统化投资（systematic investing）结合起来。我们认为，两者可以通过一些方式结合，从而更有力地为客户及其顾问实现这些结果。因此，我认为，关键其实就是能够横向审视，然后说：我们可以从这两个领域各取所长，将它们结合起来，为顾问及其客户提供更好的解决方案。

turns.en: I mean, would I would I would add to that. You know, even on your previous question, David, does the active management meet the investors' expectations? That's the that's the big piece of this, and I do think even you know, the conversation we're having around active and passive when you apply that on the fixed income side, what we hear a lot from investors is how the benchmarks or the indexes are built on the fixed income side maybe doesn't align fully with how they want to invest. And so when you have security selection on the fixed income side, where an actual portfolio manager is building a portfolio that takes into account the credit quality of the underlying issues, the duration that they're trying to accomplish, these are things that actually, you know, tie with what we're saying here. Earlier we were talking about defined outcome, we were talking about derivative income on active fixed income. That's the case as well, is you want to have a portfolio manager with their hands on the wheel that can be intentional about where they're positioning those portfolios and how they're shaping that as well to meet the client's expectations, and so kind of all of those things to Graham's point come into play with the product design to fully express what the client's trying to achieve.
turns.zh: 我还想补充一点。即使回到你前一个问题，David，主动管理能否满足投资者的预期？这是其中非常关键的一环。我们一直在讨论主动与被动，而当你把这个问题应用到固定收益领域时，我们经常听投资者说，固定收益业绩基准或指数的构建方式，可能并不完全符合他们希望采用的投资方式。因此，在固定收益领域开展证券选择时，会由真正的投资组合经理（portfolio manager）构建投资组合，考虑底层发行人的信用质量，以及他们希望达到的久期（duration）。这些实际上都与我们在这里表达的观点相呼应。前面我们谈了确定结果，也谈了主动固定收益中的衍生品收益。这方面同样如此：你希望有一位亲自掌舵的投资组合经理，能够有意识地决定这些投资组合配置在哪里，并塑造投资组合，以满足客户预期。因此，正如 Graham 所说，所有这些因素都会体现在产品设计中，从而充分表达客户希望实现的目标。

turns.en: That makes a lot of sense. I mean, you know, one of the things I hear when I track active manager performance is, you know, bond managers are almost have a cheat code just because of the way the indexes are set up. So obviously, you know, it makes a lot of sense. And you know, these products do bring a new element to that as well. And if we kind of stay on the topic of innovation, you know, Brian is active each have innovation become better at solving investor problems? Or do you think this might even be a trick question? Do you think competition has led the industry to create more products that investors actually need?
turns.zh: 这非常有道理。我在跟踪主动管理人业绩时经常听到一种说法：债券管理人几乎像是掌握了“作弊码”，原因就在于指数的构建方式。所以，这显然很有道理，而这些产品也为此增添了新的元素。如果继续谈创新，Brian，主动型 ETF 的创新是否已经更善于解决投资者的问题？或者你认为这甚至可能是个陷阱问题？你认为竞争是否促使行业创造了更多投资者真正需要的产品？

turns.en: Yeah, well, look, you know I'm always in the innovation camp, and you know, I'll remind us some history lessons that we all love. The you know, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, the first index was built in the eighteen nineties. The SMP was built in the nineteen twenties. It wasn't expanded to five hundred securities until you know, the nineteen fifties. It wasn't put into an ETF until nineteen ninety three. You know, that means we got to buy into the fact that we haven't invented anything better for the last one hundred years. And I just don't buy that. And you know, what I think we're trying to express here and the comments that Graham and I are saying, is is that innovation is continuing to happen, and product innovation is all around making outcomes for the investors better. And so all of the different tools create different different varieties. You know, if we were painting a picture and we said you only had, you know, two colors to paint it with, you could only express it in so many ways. But if we gave you the variety of ten thousand different pictures and the way that we have, you know, across kind of the ETF landscape, you can pick all of the precise colors so that you can paint a more vivid picture that you're trying to that you're trying to deliver as an artist, if you will, or a portfolio constructor as it as it may be. And so, you know, I don't think there will ever be too many I think firms like ours need to be really thoughtful and disciplined about what product we do bring We've got a history of retiring products if they don't make sense, and you know, I think that's a healthy part of the industry as well. It's a high bar for us to being a product we do. We do put a tremendous amount of thought into the products that we deliver, but that innovation making sure that we're taking the best of what we think we can deliver that's differentiated in the market, and then making that available to investors to build or paint that picture as it may be. That's that's what gets us excited.
turns.zh: 是的。坦率地说，我始终属于支持创新的一派。我想提醒大家回顾一些我们都很熟悉的历史：Dow Jones Industrial Average 这个最早的指数创立于 19 世纪 90 年代，S&P 创立于 20 世纪 20 年代，直到 20 世纪 50 年代才扩展到 500 只证券，直到 1993 年才被纳入一只 ETF。也就是说，我们必须接受这样一种观点：过去 100 年来，我们没有发明出任何更好的东西。但我根本不认同这一点。我认为，Graham 和我刚才想表达的是，创新仍在继续发生，而产品创新的核心就是为投资者带来更好的结果。所有这些不同工具创造了不同的选择。假设我们在画一幅画，而你只有两种颜色可用，那么表达方式就非常有限。但如果我们给你一万种不同的颜料——正如整个 ETF 领域提供的那样——你就可以挑选所有精确的颜色，绘出一幅更生动的画。你可以把自己看作一名艺术家，或者也可以说是一名从事投资组合构建（portfolio construction）的人。我不认为产品会多到过头。不过，我认为像我们这样的公司需要以非常审慎、自律的方式决定推出什么产品。我们有过在产品不再合理时将其终止的历史，我认为这也是行业健康发展的一部分。对我们来说，推出产品的门槛很高。我们确实会对所交付的产品进行极其深入的思考。但创新意味着确保我们拿出自己认为能够提供、而且在市场上具有差异化的最佳能力，再把它提供给投资者，让他们得以构建——或者说绘制——那幅图景。正是这一点让我们感到兴奋。

turns.en: So in addition to you know, maybe too many products, my other point would be, you know, could too much innovation lead to you know, you know, solving specific investor needs without you know, could portfolio has become unnecessarily complicated. So maybe this is a question for you, Graham. Do you think that's a possibility, not not necessarily just you know, just this would be like across the industry, not you know, for a firm or anything like that.
turns.zh: 除了产品可能过多以外，我的另一个问题是，过度创新会不会导致产品只解决特定的投资者需求，却让投资组合变得不必要地复杂？Graham，也许这个问题适合由你来回答。你认为有这种可能吗？我说的并不只是某家公司，而是整个行业。

turns.en: Yeah, it's a good question, David.
turns.zh: 是的，这是个好问题，David。

turns.en: I think from my perspective, what is complex for someone is simple for someone else, And a lot of times what it comes down.
turns.zh: 从我的角度看，对一个人来说复杂的东西，对另一个人来说可能很简单。很多时候，归根结底——

turns.en: To is education.
turns.zh: 在于教育。

turns.en: If I think back to when we first brought the buffer ETFs back in twenty eighteen, there wasn't a whole lot of appetite or knowledge about flex options and wait, how are you putting flex options in the CTF? And then what are these four or five options positions? And what's the strike price? And just having to educate advisors about, hey, you know what that option is. It's essentially the same thing as owning the S and P five hundred. Oh okay, I understand what that means. And so helping people understand to take them along the journey, I think is going to be the most important thing, and that's going to be something that we will remain committed to doing here as part of Goldman Sachs is to make sure that we're walking side by side with advisors, educating them on how these products work, how to use them when they'll work well when they may not. And I think that's one of the things that going back to your earlier question about just the massive proliferation proliferation of products, well, a lot of it's going to be based off of education, helping advisors understand and if they don't, you're going to see record closures, which again, you have record launches, you have record closures right now, and so we're gonna let the market dictate what they want. But we feel like we're going to have We're going to be in a very strong position because we're going to be focused on educating advisors on how to use these products and to better understand that, you know what. It sounds very complicated, but when you boil it down to its parts, it's actually very simple. And so I think today people look at buffer ETFs and say, oh, no, I understand that nine years ago they did not understand buffer ets. And so that's what we're going to be committed to doing on a go forward basis for any of the new products that we bring to market.
turns.zh: 回想我们在 2018 年首次推出缓冲型 ETF 时，市场对 FLEX 期权并没有太大兴趣，也不太了解。人们会问：“等等，你们怎么把 FLEX 期权放进 ETF 里的？还有，这四五个期权（option）头寸是什么？行权价是多少？”我们需要教育顾问，让他们明白：“你知道吗，这个期权本质上和持有 S&P 500 是一回事。”“哦，好的，我明白了。”因此，帮助人们理解并陪伴他们走过这一过程，将是最重要的事情。我认为，作为 Goldman Sachs 的一员，我们将继续致力于此，确保与顾问并肩前行，向他们讲解这些产品如何运作、如何使用、什么时候表现良好，以及什么时候可能表现不佳。回到你之前关于产品大规模激增的问题，我认为这也是其中一个关键点。很多事情都将取决于教育，即帮助顾问理解；如果他们不理解，你就会看到创纪录的产品关闭数量。事实上，现在产品发行量创纪录，关闭量也创纪录。因此，我们会让市场决定它想要什么。但我们认为自己将处于非常有利的位置，因为我们会专注于教育顾问如何使用这些产品，并让他们更好地理解：它听起来非常复杂，但当你把它拆解成各个组成部分时，其实非常简单。如今，人们看到缓冲型 ETF 会说：“哦，我明白了。”9 年前，他们并不了解缓冲型 ETF。因此，今后我们把任何新产品推向市场时，都将继续致力于这项工作。

turns.en: Okay, fair enough, Brian, What do you think the biggest MI misconception is?
turns.zh: 好的，有道理。Brian，你认为投资者对于主动管理仍然存在的最大误解是什么？

turns.en: One?
turns.zh: 哪一个？

turns.en: Do you think investors still have about active management? You know, this could be any you know, active management in general.
turns.zh: 可以是对主动管理总体上的任何误解。

turns.en: Yeah, I'm you know. I think you asked the question earlier and it was kind of like the biggest misconception is how narrowly it's kind of defined in the media in a number of different ways. I think that, as you know, we have conversations like this one you know, where you help educate investors to think more broadly about the full spectrum of capabilities that are available to them. I think that that kind of challenges or adjusts that we're going to you know, misconception if you will, and becomes, you know, just a really healthy conversation where investors are aware of all the different tools. You know, nobody goes into nobody goes into a hardware store and says there's too many tools for me to do, or you know, goes into an auto zone and says there's too many tools. It's like, I need this specific tool for the specific job. And you know, I think that's what you know, Graham and I are expressing again, is like, that's how we think about these things, is bringing tools for investors. Now, I will say, you know, if you think about other things that we do across Goldman, you know, we've leaned in heavily into our models business, where we are bringing together the best of the component pieces to deliver a view on what a portfolio could look like, and we leverage our multi asset capabilities with that. We've got one of the leading ocio businesses in the world. We take that chassis and build models off of that, So investors that maybe don't want to go through and select all of those, we've got the complete kind of solution for them to build in that way. We've got partners across the industry that help deliver different platforms that allow you to pick and choose different ways to deliver that as well. And so I think as this entire ecosystem evolves over time, we're just going to continue to see more selection, more options, and better outcomes for investors.
turns.zh: 我认为，你之前其实已经问到了这个问题。最大的误解在于，媒体以多种方式对主动管理作了过于狭窄的定义。我认为，当我们进行这样的讨论，而你帮助投资者更广泛地思考他们可以获得的完整能力谱系时，这就会挑战或纠正这种误解，并形成非常健康的讨论，让投资者了解所有不同工具。没有人走进五金店后会说：“这里的工具太多，我没法干活。”也没有人走进 AutoZone 后说：“这里工具太多了。”实际情况是：“我要用这种特定工具来完成这项特定工作。”我认为，这也是 Graham 和我再次表达的观点：我们看待这些产品的方式，就是为投资者提供工具。不过我还想说，如果你看看我们在 Goldman Sachs 开展的其他业务，就会发现我们大力投入了模型组合业务，把最优秀的组成部分汇集起来，就投资组合可以呈现的样貌提供一种观点，并在其中运用我们的多资产能力。我们拥有全球领先的外包首席投资官业务（outsourced chief investment officer, OCIO）之一，并以这一架构为基础构建模型组合。因此，对于可能不想亲自逐一挑选所有产品的投资者，我们有完整的解决方案，帮助他们以这种方式构建投资组合。我们在整个行业还有合作伙伴，可以提供不同平台，让你以不同方式挑选并交付这些方案。因此，我认为，随着整个生态系统不断演变，我们只会看到更多选择、更多选项，以及更好的投资者结果。

turns.en: Okay, Griham, Since you know with all these new products coming, do you think expectations from advisors have changed over the past few years and what they can expect from active managers.
turns.zh: 好的。Graham，随着所有这些新产品不断涌现，你认为过去几年里，顾问的期望以及他们对主动管理人的期待发生变化了吗？

turns.en: One hundred percent? And I think going back to this solutions oriented mindset that we've we've brought. First it was with the buffers of how how do I protect my portfolio and stay invested in equities? Okay, well those are the buffer ETFs. You can have some of the upside and still have no levels of downside protection. Then involved to well, you know what, how do we protect all of my assets? Well, you know we can do that. We can do that with options, we can have one hundred percent downside protection. We can give you an alternative to just stand on the sidelines with cash. Then it was, well, if bonds aren't always going to be able to protect me or hedge, what other solutions do you have? Well, that's where we have these dual directional ETFs that you know, in certain down markets you will make money. And these are the types of things that I think advisors are looking for, these specific types of solutions in today's market, especially when you think about building a portfolio the sixty forty. Really any advisor can do that, and so they're looking to deliver value to their clients, and so how can they meet that demand from clients is to give them these unique types of solutions to say, hey, we're very thoughtful about your concern about downside risk management. We have bonds in there, but you know what, we've added these dual direction and buffer ETFs to make a more holistic risk managed strategy. And so I think again it's just going to be this continued evolution of what other solutions can we build to meet advisors needs, to meet their clients' needs, and ultimately to build better outcomes for them.
turns.zh: 百分之百。我认为，这又回到了我们带来的面向解决方案的思维方式。最初是缓冲产品：我如何既保护投资组合，又继续投资股票？答案就是缓冲型 ETF。你可以获得一部分上涨收益，同时仍然拥有已知水平的下行保护。后来问题演变成：“怎样才能保护我的全部资产？”我们同样可以做到，可以通过期权实现 100% 的下行保护，为你提供一种替代方案，而不是只能持有现金、留在场外。之后的问题又变成：“如果债券不一定总能保护我或提供对冲，你们还有什么其他解决方案？”这就轮到了双向 ETF。在某些下跌市场中，你确实可以通过它们赚钱。我认为，顾问在今天的市场上寻找的正是这些具体类型的解决方案。尤其是考虑到投资组合构建中的 60/40 组合，实际上任何顾问都能做，所以他们希望为客户提供价值。那么，他们如何满足客户的这种需求呢？就是给客户提供这些独特的解决方案，并告诉他们：“我们非常认真地考虑了你对下行风险管理的担忧。组合里有债券，但我们还加入了双向 ETF 和缓冲型 ETF，从而打造一种更全面的风险管理策略。”因此我还是认为，这将是一个持续演变的过程：我们还能构建哪些其他解决方案，以满足顾问的需求、满足其客户的需求，并最终为他们实现更好的结果。

turns.en: I mean, if I could just add to kind of gram's you know comment there. You know, one of the things that we spend a lot of time talking about Graham and I and the and the and the rest of the folks here, you know, kind of at Goldman is what does it take to be an excellent active manager and to really differentiate yourself and to boil it down, we think about three different components. One is technology. You have to have great technology in order to do the research, to do the trading, to do all the different components that go into it. You have to have great data. Increasingly in an AI first world, you need the data sets that you have and rich and do all of these different things that can help you have views on the marketplace and where it's going. And then you need to take that technology in that data and you need to give it to the best people. And we've got over a thousand professional investors globally that we give that technology and that data too that help us build these active solutions for investors. And we do think that that differentiates us from the rest of the marketplace because of what we've invested in technology, the types of data that we have, and how we prosecute that data, and then the people that we deliver and I think all of those things tie together, particularly with the rest of the conversation we've been having here as far as setting Goldman in a good position to help deliver those outcomes for investors. And you know, if I'm an investor, or an advisor, an individual, I want to make sure that I'm thinking about what is the firm doing, what's behind the scenes. So fine, I can search for the ticker, but I want to understand what the platform is that I'm accessing, and who's behind that, what's the infrastructure, And that's where I think that investors maybe should be you know, spending some of their time as well.
turns.zh: 我想对 Graham 的这番话再补充一点。Graham、我和 Goldman Sachs 的其他同事经常花大量时间讨论：成为优秀的主动管理人、真正实现差异化，需要具备什么？概括起来，我们考虑三个不同要素。第一是技术。你必须拥有出色的技术，才能开展研究、进行交易，并完成其中涉及的所有不同环节。第二是出色的数据。在一个人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI）优先的世界里，数据集变得越来越重要。你需要能够丰富数据并进行各种处理，从而帮助你形成对市场及其走向的看法。第三，你需要把这些技术和数据交给最优秀的人才。我们在全球拥有超过 1,000 名专业投资者，我们把这些技术和数据交给他们，帮助我们为投资者构建这些主动解决方案。我们确实认为，凭借我们在技术上的投入、拥有的数据类型、处理这些数据的方式，以及我们所提供的人才，我们能够区别于市场上的其他参与者。我认为，所有这些因素相互联系，尤其是结合我们刚才的其他讨论，它们让 Goldman Sachs 处于有利位置，能够帮助投资者实现这些结果。如果我是投资者——无论是顾问还是个人——我都会确保自己思考这家公司在做什么、幕后有什么。没错，我可以搜索基金代码，但我还想了解自己正在使用的是什么平台，背后是谁，有什么样的基础设施。我认为，投资者或许也应该在这方面投入一些时间。

turns.en: Okay, And if we go, you know, if we just think about the future for a bit, so Brian, if we think about the next decade, and you know, I want to think about active management in general relative to passive. We all know, you know, with the advent or, with active you know, gaining so much momentum over the last few years, people seem to forget the passive is still seeing a lot of flows, you know s and P five hundred index funds. Do you think the greatest value active will provide is in these specialized products over the next decade?
turns.zh: 好的。如果我们稍微展望一下未来，Brian，假设我们思考未来十年，并把主动管理总体上与被动投资进行比较。我们都知道，随着主动管理在过去几年获得如此强劲的发展势头，人们似乎忘了被动投资仍在吸引大量资金流入，比如 S&P 500 指数基金。你认为，未来十年主动管理提供的最大价值会来自这些专业化产品吗？

turns.en: No, I think it's going to be I think it's going to be substantial because you know, so if you if you look at the entire forty act space, that's north of forty trillion dollars inclusive of active mutu funds, passive ets, and active ets, right, And so what we're seeing is, you know, steadily those assets are evolving. Muta funds still play a big role, and we've got a franchise of muta funds that we're very proud of and you know, continues to grow in a very healthy way. We have seen kind of the etf rapper continue to grow at a very fast pace. It's kind of like this this new technology, if you will. I know, it's been around for a number of years, but it's still evolving in that way. And in fact, it's you know, ETFs in the US big round numbers are like seventeen trillion dollars of that forty trillion, and so even though they've been around since nineteen ninety three, they're still not fifty percent of the market space. And indeed, that other kind of two thirds, if you will, is in active mutual funds. And I think the markets are relatively efficient, meaning that investors that are using those to get active, you know, performance in their portfolios are going to start to see that they've got more selection now both muta funds, ETFs, indeed separately managed accounts and other things that are out there. And so over time, I think that mix will just continue to evolve. Investors will look for the investment outcome that they're trying to achieve, whether that's the buffer, like Graham was talking about a floor, an income oriented strategy outperforming a benchmark on the fixed income side. On the active small cap space where we've got a really exciting etfgsc our small cap where we have a fantastic portfolio manager there using all of those different strategies and then figuring out what's the right way to access that, maybe through a mutual fund, maybe through an ETF, maybe through a separate manage account, and so you have all of these things that are converging and so you know, look, the good news is is that this wealth space continues to grow rapidly. That's a very exciting area. There's more and more capabilities for more people to get involved and to be invested, and now there's all of these different tools for them to use to build that perfect portfolio. So I think it's a really exciting time. And so as we look forward, I think we're just scratching the surface on the innovation that we're going to see, the growth that we're going to see, and active is going to play a huge part in the in the overall ecosystem.
turns.zh: 不，我认为主动管理的影响将会非常大。如果观察整个《1940 年投资公司法》所涵盖的市场，其规模超过 40 万亿美元，包括主动型共同基金、被动型 ETF 和主动型 ETF。我们看到这些资产在稳步演变。共同基金仍然发挥着重要作用；我们拥有一项引以为豪的共同基金业务，而且它继续以非常健康的方式增长。我们确实看到，ETF 载体继续以非常快的速度增长。如果愿意，可以把它看作一种新技术。我知道 ETF 已经存在很多年，但它仍在以这种方式演变。事实上，以美国市场的大致数字计算，在这 40 万亿美元中，ETF 约占 17 万亿美元。因此，尽管 ETF 自 1993 年就已经存在，但仍未占到市场空间的 50%。实际上，其余约三分之二的资产都在主动型共同基金中。我认为市场相对有效率，这意味着，使用这些产品在投资组合中获取主动管理业绩的投资者会开始看到，他们现在拥有更多选择，包括共同基金、ETF，甚至独立管理账户（separately managed account）以及其他工具。因此，随着时间推移，我认为这种组合只会继续演变。投资者会寻找自己希望实现的投资结果，无论是 Graham 所说的缓冲、保底线、收益导向策略，还是在固定收益领域跑赢业绩基准。再比如主动管理的小盘股（small cap）领域，我们有一只令人非常振奋的小盘股 ETF GSC，由一位出色的投资组合经理运用所有这些不同策略来管理。随后，投资者还要确定获取这种能力的正确方式：可能通过共同基金，可能通过 ETF，也可能通过独立管理账户。所有这些都在趋于融合。好消息是，财富管理市场仍在快速增长，这是一个令人非常振奋的领域。越来越多人可以获得越来越多的能力，可以参与进来并进行投资；如今，他们也有所有这些不同工具来构建理想的投资组合。因此，我认为这是一个非常令人兴奋的时期。展望未来，我认为，对于我们将看到的创新和增长而言，现在还只是刚刚触及表面；主动管理将在整个生态系统中发挥巨大作用。

turns.en: Okay, now that makes a lot of sense, you know, so obviously we're going to be watching Graham. You think it really is like education, you know, getting more investors accustomed to these type of strategies.
turns.zh: 好的，这很有道理，所以我们显然会继续关注。Graham，我想问的是，对于这类产品的下一阶段增长，什么因素会起到定义作用？我本来想说“挑战”，但不确定这是不是正确的词。你认为关键确实在于教育，让更多投资者习惯这类策略吗？

turns.en: Yeah, I really do, and I think that's why we're so focused on the education side of things. What we have found is if you can take a payoff that maybe has been available in other rappers in the past, and what we found is if it's available in one rapper, there's a good chance that if we can put in the ETF, there's going to be demand for that as well. Now there's a lot of advisors that have maybe never used those payoffs before in other rappers, but once it becomes available in an ETF, there's they say, hey, you know what, that's actually really interesting. I never took a look at you know, I don't use insurance products, for example, but now that's an ETF, I can understand why I would want to use this in my in my client's portfolios. And so I think everything goes back to the education of just making sure the advisors understand what they're owning when it's going to work well, the benefits, the scenarios where maybe it's not going to perform as well. But that's one of the beauties of defined outcome investing is because you know before you invest, these are the markets it's going to do really well. In the markets are down, you know exactly what you're going to get. And so it's that transparency that they're also going to continue to receive what these types of payoffs.
turns.zh: 是的，我确实这样认为，这正是我们如此专注于教育工作的原因。我们发现，如果某种收益结构过去曾通过其他载体提供，那么只要它能在一种载体中实现，就很有可能也能放进 ETF，并且同样会有需求。有很多顾问过去可能从未通过其他载体使用过这些收益结构，但一旦它可以通过 ETF 获取，他们就会说：“你知道吗，这真的很有意思。比如，我以前从未研究过这类产品，也不使用保险产品；但现在它变成了 ETF，我能理解为什么自己会想在客户的投资组合中使用它。”因此，我认为一切又回到了教育：确保顾问了解自己持有什么、它什么时候表现良好、有哪些优势，以及在哪些情景下可能表现不那么好。不过，确定结果型投资的一个优点在于，你投资之前就知道它会在哪些市场中表现得非常好；市场下跌时，你也确切知道自己会得到什么。因此，借助这类收益结构，他们也会继续获得这种透明度。

turns.en: I'll go first, So you know, I'll take a different road so that Graham can you know, talk about what he wants to talk about, probably in the defined outcome space and the amazing investment the Golden's made an innovator. But you know, we touched on in a second ago. You know, we've launched a Muni suite of products Team U, We've ACT, We've we've launched Broader, you know Active Fixed Income and Giggle, g I, g L and g Bond and all of these other ones that have you know, known portfolio managers that run substantial books, that are that are kind of experts in their in their space, that now have these available in the in the ETF wrapper. And I do think that as investors get more comfortable with understanding how fixed income ETFs work, and then indeed how active fixed income ETFs work, and all the efficiencies that come when you think about that, I think that the appreciation for the intro day liquidity of a fixed income portfolio bonds, the immediate diversification UH that comes with buying one ticker that gives you access to hundreds or sometimes thousands of of different bonds. I do think that as investors understand that more deeply, we're just going to see, you know, continued growth in that area, and that that fixed income is going to be an area where investors should you know, be educated by a couple of tickers. I understand how a trades and over time, you know, we're going to see that snowball. Okay, but about you Graham.
turns.zh: 我先说。我要换一条思路，这样 Graham 就可以谈他想谈的内容，或许是确定结果领域，以及 Goldman Sachs 对 Innovator 所做的重大投资。不过，我们刚才已经简单提到，我认为主动固定收益领域仍然极其有意思。我们已经证明，如果拥有出色的投资组合管理，以及构建投资组合并以特定方式塑造组合的能力，就可以真正带来不一样的结果。现在市场上也有各种主动型 ETF。我们推出了市政债券（municipal bond）产品系列 Team U，也推出了 ACT；还推出了更广泛的主动固定收益产品，包括 Giggle、G I、G L 和 G Bond，以及其他各种产品。这些产品由知名投资组合经理管理，他们管理着规模可观的投资组合，是各自领域的专家，而这些产品现在已经可以通过 ETF 载体获取。我确实认为，随着投资者更熟悉固定收益 ETF 的运作方式，继而更了解主动固定收益 ETF 的运作方式，并认识到由此带来的所有效率优势，我们会看到他们更加欣赏固定收益投资组合的日内流动性（liquidity）；他们也会更加欣赏即时的分散化（diversification），因为只需买入一个基金代码，就能投资数百只、有时甚至数千只不同的债券；此外，还有交易所内往来交易的二级市场效率，以及能够降低价差、提高获取此类敞口效率的一级市场。我确实认为，随着投资者对此有更深入的了解，我们只会看到这个领域继续增长，而固定收益将成为投资者应该了解的一个领域。买几个基金代码，了解它们如何交易；随着时间推移，我们会看到这种趋势像滚雪球一样发展。好的，Graham，你怎么看？

turns.en: Yeah, David, I would say I would one hundred percent agree with Brian. And it's funny we talk about fixed income being an area too where we think there's a lot of opportunity to innovate within that space. But I think one of the trends that's underappreciated is this idea that a lot of these payoffs that have been available, they've been available off exchange, and so by placing it, you know, taking those payoffs and putting them on the exchange, you have the liquidity, the transparency, the tax efficiency, and so I think you're going to continue to see that movement continue that where there's these payoffs that again, whether it's in another institution insurance company that's structuring these types of payoffs, if you can figure out how to put it in the ETF wrapper, if you can figure out how to put it on exchange, it adds that transparency, it adds more to liquidity. If anything, what we found is sometimes people think that we really compete with other areas, other product wrappers. If anything, we compliment them very well because we bring more attention to the fact that, you know what, some of these defined payoffs, they're really really powerful. And I had never looked at a structured note before, and so now I'm going to start pairing these together. And so here at Goldman Sachs we're one of the largest issuers of structured notes as well, and so these two can coexist, each have their own benefits. But I think you're going to continue to see this evolution of off exchange instruments and payoffs. If you can figure out how to put them on exchange. I think there's going to be a lot of additional innovation that can be unlocked.
turns.zh: 是的，David，我百分之百赞同 Brian。说起来很有意思，我们也在谈论固定收益，认为这是一个存在大量创新机会的领域。但我认为，有一个未获充分重视的趋势：很多这类收益结构过去其实已经存在，只不过是在交易所外提供。把这些收益结构放到交易所交易，就能获得流动性、透明度和税务效率。因此，我认为这一迁移会继续发展。无论这类收益结构来自其他机构，还是由保险公司设计，只要你能想办法把它放进 ETF 载体，并放到交易所交易，就能提高透明度和流动性。我认为，这会释放出大量额外创新。我们还发现，有时人们认为我们实际上是在与其他领域、其他产品载体竞争。事实恰恰相反，我们与它们形成了很好的互补，因为我们让更多人注意到，有些确定收益结构确实非常强大。人们会说：“我以前从未研究过结构性票据（structured note），所以现在我要开始把这些产品搭配起来。”Goldman Sachs 也是最大的结构性票据发行人之一，因此二者可以共存，各有自身优势。但我认为，我们将继续看到交易所外工具和收益结构发生这种演变。如果你能想办法把它们放到交易所交易，我认为就可以释放大量额外创新。

turns.zh: 我先说，我就沿用 Brian 回答上一个问题时讨论的内容。我认为变化会发生在固定收益领域，这里将出现大量创新。从很多方面来说，固定收益在媒体讨论中一直被忽视，你看不到太多炒作。不过现实是，我们可以讨论 60/40 组合正在发生变化——它确实如此。现在正是重新思考如何在 60/40 组合之外构建投资组合的绝佳时机。但现实是，绝大部分客户资金仍然流向债券。那么，如何在债券领域实现更好的结果？如何对冲部分下行风险？如何提高部分上行收益率？通过开展大量这种定制，我认为固定收益这一类别将出现很多创新。
